quarterly_data.quarter: Sanofi press release: Press Release: Sanofi and Regeneron expand global Alliance (10-01-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Sanofi and Regeneron expanded their antibody Alliance (the collaboration behind Dupixent): under the expanded license and collaboration agreement the companies will co-develop and co-commercialize four new long-acting, Regeneron-invented antibodies targeting IL-13, IL-4xIL-13 (bispecific), IL-4 and IL-4R alpha. The IL-13 antibody REGN20423 is currently in a phase 1 clinical study for atopic dermatitis, and the other three antibodies are expected to enter clinical studies in 2027. Regeneron also gets an option to include Sanofi's lunsekimig (bispecific Nanobody VHH targeting TSLP and IL-13), exercisable upon completion of its phase 3 studies in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. Regeneron receives a $1 billion upfront payment from Sanofi, with potential development, regulatory and commercial milestones of up to an additional $7 billion; development and commercialization costs are shared and future profits split 50:50 globally, with Regeneron leading R&D and Sanofi leading global commercial efforts. The existing Dupixent profit-sharing agreement does not change, and the companies have settled their prior collaboration-related litigation. CEO Belen Garijo called it 'a deliberate first step in igniting Sanofi's innovation engine'.
quarterly_data.figure: four new long-acting antibodies; REGN20423 in phase 1 (atopic dermatitis), three others to enter clinic in 2027; $1 billion upfront, up to $7 billion milestones; 50:50 profit split
